page_title: Rider: the cross-platform .NET and game development IDE from JetBrains

sources.entry: Rider - Cross-platform C# IDE with Resharper features.

summary.name: JetBrains Rider
summary.one_liner: Rider is JetBrains' cross-platform IDE for .NET, ASP.NET Core, and game development (Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot), with integrated tools for working alongside AI coding agents.
use_cases: Developing .NET and ASP.NET Core web services and APIs
Building and debugging Unity or Unreal Engine games in C#/C++
Maintaining long-lived WinForms, WPF, or MAUI enterprise applications
Running AI coding agents alongside a .NET codebase and reviewing their changes
Developing a .NET backend together with a React, Angular, or Vue frontend
summary.what_it_does: Rider is a .NET and game development IDE that runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It resolves the whole codebase (types, usages, dependencies, framework conventions) and provides refactorings, inspections, a debugger, profiler, test runner, database tools, and Git support. It supports ASP.NET Core, Blazor, MAUI, EF Core, Aspire, and JavaScript/TypeScript frontends such as React, Angular, and Vue. For games it offers engine-aware analysis, navigation, and debugging for Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot, and custom engines. The page also describes integration with AI agents (such as Junie, Claude Agent, Codex, and GitHub Copilot) that can use Rider's refactorings and debugger, and session tracking for running agents.
notable: Free for individual non-commercial use; commercial use needs a paid license
Standalone IDE, or bundled in dotUltimate with ReSharper, dotTrace, dotMemory, dotCover and JetBrains AI credits
Works without AI: completion, refactoring, debugger and test runner are available without agents
Engine-aware support for Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot and custom engines
caveats: Commercial development requires a paid license; free tier is for non-commercial use only
Profiling and some features depend on the dotUltimate bundle or platform-specific requirements
Available agent models and features depend on the specific integration
